clue.text: Continued to exert influence on English lecturer

parts.note: to press someone is to bring influence or pressure to bear on them
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone kept leaning on an English lecturer to get their way.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to keep going despite difficulty, a phrasal synonym for carried on.

clue.text: City which is a centre for the micrometer

indicators.note: the letters wanted sit at the very heart of the long measuring-instrument word that follows

explanation.surface: A city is claimed to be the hub of the precision measuring trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre for' points to the four letters in the middle of 'micrometer', between MIC and TER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian capital is a city.

clue.text: Perceptive son meets Doone leader before end of May

parts.note: Sir Ensor Doone is head of the outlaw Doone clan in Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone

indicators.note: only the final letter of the month name is taken

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted son meets the head of an outlaw clan just before May ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doone leader' looks like Carver or the first letter D, but it is Sir Ensor Doone, the clan chief in Lorna Doone; 'meets' and 'before' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensory relates to the senses, the faculties of perception.

clue.text: Sensing distress in US navy personnel

indicators.note: distress here works as a verb, the letters being knocked about and set in a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors in the American fleet pick up signals of trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensigns are the most junior commissioned officers in the United States Navy.

clue.text: Appeal to archdeacon for a heater

parts.note: O is the vocative cry of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a senior cleric for a fire to warm the vicarage.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is a heated enclosed chamber used for cooking, so a kind of heater.

clue.text: Now is the time to make a donation

definitions.meaning: the current instant, this very time

definitions.text: the time to make a donation
definitions.meaning: read literally, the instant when a gift is handed over

explanation.surface: A charity appeal urges giving immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means right now, and read as two words it is the occasion of giving a gift.

clue.text: Amateur festival charity performance is a perk

parts.note: the Fringe is the open-access festival running alongside the Edinburgh International Festival
a benefit is a show staged to raise funds for a cause or person

explanation.surface: Getting into an amateur festival's charity show is a nice bonus of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Fringe is the big open festival held each August in Scotland's capital, alongside the official one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe benefit is an extra given with a job besides wages, such as a company car.

clue.text: Father's no more disposed to be sincere

indicators.note: disposed in its sense of arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken with its letters as written, the S included

explanation.surface: Dad is no longer inclined to mean what he says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges all thirteen letters of FATHERS NO MORE; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Words said from the depths of feeling are heartfelt and genuine.

clue.text: Call for a path to be made tidy

definitions.meaning: a shout asking people to step aside and open up a route
to remove clutter and put things in order

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for a route to be opened and the place neatened.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry asking for passage, and also a phrasal verb meaning to remove things after a meal or task.

clue.text: Acceptance of order to sleep easy

indicators.note: order as a verb, telling us to put these letters into a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: A doctor's instruction to rest well is gratefully taken up.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the polite phrase used to accept an offer of something.

clue.text: State indistinctly that the final odds are one pound

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound
I is the Roman numeral for one
SP, the starting price, is the last odds on offer before a race begins

explanation.surface: A bookie mumbles that the closing price is one pound.
explanation.walkthrough: In British betting the starting price (SP) is the final odds when the race starts; the pieces come in the reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment that turns s sounds into th makes words come out unclearly.

clue.text: Smith's business is to counterfeit money

definitions.meaning: a blacksmith's workshop with its furnace and anvil

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's real trade is faking cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A smithy's hearth for working metal, and a verb meaning to make a fraudulent copy.

clue.text: First cardinal to go round Cape long ago

indicators.note: the number word is placed around the abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: one is the first of the cardinal numbers
C is the standard abbreviation for Cape on maps

explanation.surface: Long ago the first cardinal set off to sail round the Cape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman, but it is a cardinal number.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, formerly.

clue.text: Escort you and me to the lady

parts.note: us is the pronoun for the speaker together with the listener
her is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Accompany the two of us over to the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats or into a room, as an attendant.

clue.text: Hesitate to give employment to secretary

parts.note: PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
employment in the sense of making use of something

explanation.surface: A boss hesitates over taking on a secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: To pause is to stop briefly, holding back before acting.

clue.text: It may set many free

indicators.note: free as in loose, the letters let go to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A general pardon could release a great number of prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges SET MANY, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An official pardon releases groups of offenders from prosecution or prison.

clue.text: Get fish in to eat for a complete change

indicators.note: the fish word is placed within the eating word

parts.note: to sup is to take a meal, especially supper
hake is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Bringing fish into the diet makes for a total change of routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shake-up is a radical reorganisation, as of a company or team.

clue.text: Unambitious idiot swallows lime squash

indicators.note: the fool word takes the scrambled fruit inside it, like food going down

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: squash in the sense of crush, mashing the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A lazy fool gulps down a lime cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like the drink, but here it is the anagram signal working on 'lime', and 'swallows' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no goals or purpose drifts without direction.

clue.text: Drag one's feet prior to dealing

definitions.meaning: to walk without lifting the feet properly
what a card player does to the pack before dealing

explanation.surface: A card player stalls before handing out the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a scraping walk and the mixing of a pack of cards before play.

clue.text: To past student display of emotion is offensive

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil
making a scene is a public emotional outburst

explanation.surface: A former pupil's emotional outburst causes offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or grossly offensive to accepted standards.

clue.text: He is commissioned to bid about one hundred

indicators.note: the bid word goes around the numerals, enclosing them

parts.note: an offer is a bid, as at auction
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A man is commissioned to make an offer of about a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commissioned' sounds like hired to do a job, but it means holding a commission in the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A military officer holds a commission granted by the head of state.

clue.text: Should it always include the Marines?

definitions.text: Should it always include the Marines?

indicators.note: the word for always holds the Marines abbreviation inside it

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for always or ever
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether land forces ought to take in the Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Marines belong to the Royal Navy, hence the question.
explanation.definitionFit: The land-fighting service is the force asked about.

clue.text: The old East Kents are experts

definitions.meaning: the former Royal East Kent Regiment, nicknamed for its buff-coloured facings
enthusiasts with great knowledge of a subject

explanation.surface: Veterans of an old Kent regiment are authorities on the subject.
explanation.walkthrough: The Buffs were a British army regiment from Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic regimental nickname and an informal word for keen knowledgeable fans.

clue.text: Lord Murray's eyeglass

definitions.meaning: Len Murray, TUC leader, became Lord Murray
a single glass worn to aid sight

explanation.surface: A peer's monocle.
explanation.walkthrough: Len Murray led Britain's Trades Union Congress in the 1970s and was made a life peer.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive of a trade unionist's first name, and the curved glass that focuses light.

clue.text: Spare container with hard interior

indicators.note: the hardness letter is placed in the middle of the container word

parts.note: a tin is a metal container
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A spare box has a hard lining.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can mean lean or slender, as in a spare frame.

clue.text: Day on a Welsh island

parts.note: Mon is the short form of Monday

explanation.surface: A day out on an island off Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Mona is the old Latin name for Anglesey, off the north coast of Wales.

clue.text: Apparently where the Eiger mountaineer is most exposed

definitions.text: where the Eiger mountaineer is most exposed
definitions.meaning: the Eiger's notorious north wall leaves climbers dangling on the sheer rock

explanation.surface: Climbers on the Eiger seem to be at their most vulnerable on its sheer side.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning seemingly, and literally a climber clinging on a mountain wall.

clue.text: Withdrawing to a monastery, perhaps

definitions.meaning: falling back, as a defeated army does
gone away for quiet spiritual reflection

explanation.surface: Someone is withdrawing to a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: An army falling back, and someone away on a spiritual retreat.
